messages:
sarah-sales: Quick heads up — Semantix asking for a short POC: customer-managed keys (BYOK) + HSM-backed encryption, but their network only allows outbound to a whitelisted IP range and no inbound. They want to verify key usage latency + rotation flow. Any blockers?

ashley-se: Noted. Do we know which HSM vendor/protocol they expect (KMIP, PKCS#11, CloudHSM API)? Also need exact egress IPs and whether they can open a stable VPN/PrivateLink.

sarah-sales: They said 'any HSM provider' but prefer a managed cloud HSM they already use. Egress: 3 IPs (10.10.1.1/32, 10.10.1.2/32, 10.10.1.3/32) — legacy NAT gateway. No VPN allowed during POC.

dave-crypto: If there's no inbound, we'll need to run the KMS handshake from the customer to our endpoint. That works if they allow TCP to port 443/8060 depending on protocol. KMIP usually requires TLS on TCP/5696 or 5697 — can we support KMIP over TLS to unique IPs?

maria-ops: We can publish a dedicated egress proxy IP set for the POC (short lived). But two gotchas: 1) HSM proxies + mutual TLS client certs need SNI preserved; 2) If NAT is symmetric, session affinity could break long-lived TLS with KV cache.

ashley-se: For the POC success criteria we should capture: 1) end-to-end encryption of model tokens (ok), 2) key usage latency < 12ms median for sign/decrypt, 3) successful automated rotation without downtime, 4) test vectors for acceptance. Can customer provide a small perf harness we can run?

ben-mleng: Perf note — HSM round-trips add tail latency. If they expect single-request per token signing, cost skyrockets. Recommend caching wrapped DEKs at Redwood side and only call HSM for unwrap/rotate. Need their security sign-off for ephemeral DEK cache TTL (we usually suggest 10m).

dave-crypto: Agreed with DEK cache. Also need to confirm HSM supports bulk key export for rotation dry-run (we do zero-downtime rotation by double-write and gradual key cutover). If the HSM vendor forbids key duplication/export, we'll rely on rewrap flows which add latency during rotation window.

sarah-sales: They're sensitive about any cached plaintext. They want the DEK never persisted in plain inside Redwood infra. Will a wrapped DEK caching approach meet compliance?

dave-crypto: Yes — cache only wrapped DEKs (ciphertext) and keep unwrap operations in HSM. The unwrapping happens only in memory per request. Outline to customer: no plaintext at rest on Redwood.

maria-ops: Network runbook ask — Semantix must allow outbound to these hostnames/IPs: proxy1.redwood-inference.com (54.23.12.34), proxy2.redwood-inference.com (54.23.12.35). If they cannot, fallback is to run Redwood private connector in their VPC (requires VPN) or a small on-prem agent (airgap mode) which is heavier.

ashley-se: Pricing impact: direct HSM ops are billed per-signature + baseline POC connector fee. For rough estimate: expected 5k key ops/day => add ~$0.03/op => ~$150/day for HSM ops plus connector work. If we do DEK caching, HSM ops drop ~90% and cost becomes negligible compared to GPU cost.

sarah-sales: Customer asked for a sample rotation dry-run plan and a checklist for legal/security questionnaire. Can someone paste a minimal runbook + the questionnaire snippets?

dave-crypto: Runbook (high level):
1) Preflight: confirm cert thumbprints, network connectivity, test PSA vectors.
2) Schedule low-traffic window.
3) Deploy new key version in HSM, publish wrapped DEKs with new key.
4) Canary: route 1% traffic to new key for 30m, monitor errors/latency.
5) Promote, monitor 1h, then retire old key after 24h.

Security questionnaire snippet we usually supply: 
- "Where are keys generated?" -> Customer can generate in their HSM and only send wrapped keys.
- "Is plaintext ever stored?" -> No, plaintext DEKs are never persisted; only wrapped ciphertext cached.
- "Rotation procedure" -> Provide the runbook steps and verification hash.

maria-ops: Network test snippet (curl) — ask customer to validate outbound TLS to our proxy and fetch a handshake token: 
```
curl -v --tlsv1.2 https://proxy1.redwood-inference.com/handshake -H "X-Client-ID: semantix-poc"
```
They should see HTTP/200 with a JSON token.

ashley-se: Also ask them to provide a small perf harness (node/python) that does 1000 simulated unwrapps at target QPS and capture p50/p95/p99. We can run it against their HSM endpoint or our proxy depending on allowed topology.

deploy-bot: SOW TEMPLATE: https://internal.redwood/sow-templates/byo-kms-poc (shared). Please attach customer LOI and desired calendar week for POC.

sarah-sales: Plan for next steps: 1) share network IPs + allowlist request to Semantix (I'll send), 2) get HSM vendor + protocol confirmation from them, 3) send runbook + questionnaire, 4) pricing estimate with two scenarios (direct ops vs DEK caching). Who owns the runbook doc?

ashley-se: I'll draft runbook + acceptance checklist and upload to the shared folder. Expect a draft EOD tomorrow.

ben-mleng: I'll sketch perf expectations and the harness example by tomorrow AM.

dave-crypto: I'll prepare the security blurb and rotation verification artifact (sha256 signing of key metadata).

sarah-sales: Perfect — thanks all. Semantix wants to start POC next Monday if we can clear the egress IPs. I'll ping once I have their whitelist. :thumbsup:

maria-ops: FYI if they end up with symmetric NAT and no persistent outgoing IPs, we should budget time for the on-prem connector — that's a 2-3 day ops lift.

sarah-sales: noted.

ashley-se: ack :raised_hands:
